newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says extends special loans to Hanwa Bank.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says extends special loans to Hanwa Bank.

text.p: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) has extended special loans to Hanwa Bank Ltd to help it deal with repayment of deposits, a BOJ spokesman said on Thursday.

"We can't disclose the actual amount we've extended to Hanwa. However, as the BOJ governor said (this morning), we will take all possible measures to prevent a worsening of its cash flow problems," another BOJ official said.
He added that repayments to depositors at Hanwa Bank had been proceeding "normally and quietly".

BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a news conference earlier that all deposits at Hanwa would be protected and the BOJ would take all necessary steps to secure sufficient funds should a shortage for deposit repayment occur before its business was transferred to a new bank on its liquidation.
The second-tier regional bank based in western Japan was ordered to suspend all its operations except deposit withdrawals on Thursday morning because it was unable to recover bad loans.
